rubrics.rubric: Does the data audit correctly identify the Dell R760xa per-node power discrepancy where subsystem components sum to only 1,830 W but the System Total is listed as 3,500 W?
criterion: The audit must identify that for the Dell R760xa, summing the four subsystem rows (GPU 1,200 W + CPU & Memory 500 W + Storage 80 W + Networking 50 W) yields only 1,830 W.
The audit must flag that the System Total row lists 3,500 W, creating a 1,670 W gap where the System Total is almost double the subsystem sum.
The audit must note this is the inverse of the DGX H100 problem, suggesting either missing component listings or unexplained overhead, and classify it as an internal spec-sheet inconsistency.

rubrics.rubric: Does the hybrid strategy analysis correctly identify sustained vs. bursty workloads using the 500 GPU-hrs/month threshold and reallocate workloads accordingly?
criterion: The hybrid strategy analysis must query the computing_needs table to separate researchers with gpu_hours_monthly > 500 (sustained, suitable for on-prem) from those with ≤500 (bursty, suitable for cloud).

The analysis must identify that 36 of 45 total workloads exceed 500 GPU-hrs/month, including high-demand users like Dr. Kowalski (5,000 hrs), Dr. Tanaka (4,800 hrs), Dr. Ramanathan (4,500 hrs), Dr. Weber (4,200 hrs), and others.
The analysis must right-size the on-prem cluster for the sustained subset and calculate residual cloud costs for bursty workloads, resulting in a lower capital requirement than full on-prem.

rubrics.rubric: Does the sustainability scoring in the weighted matrix correctly reference LBNL report data, specifically citing PUE values by data center type (e.g., hyperscale ~1.22, midsize/colo ~1.68, small ~1.91, AI specialized ~1.14) and/or WUE data to differentiate on-prem vs. cloud sustainability?
criterion: The strategy analysis must cite specific PUE data from the LBNL 2024 Data Center Energy Usage Report, including aggregate PUE by space type in 2023: Small data centers ~1.91, Midsize/Colo ~1.68, Hyperscale ~1.22, AI Specialized ~1.14 (Figure 4.5).
The analysis must note that a university on-prem facility (midsize category, PUE ~1.5 or ~1.68 per LBNL data) is significantly less energy-efficient than hyperscale cloud providers (~1.22 PUE).
The strategy analysis should reference additional LBNL data points such as annual average PUE trends (1.6 in 2014 to ~1.4 in 2023) and/or WUE data (~0.36 L/kWh overall in 2023).
Simply mentioning 'sustainability' without specific LBNL data points constitutes a failure.

rubrics.rubric: Does the data audit identify researchers from the survey database whose per-workload memory or storage needs exceed what the proposed cluster provides per node?
criterion: The data audit must cross-reference computing_needs against cluster specs: DGX H100 provides 2 TB system memory and 640 GB GPU memory (80 GB × 8 GPUs) per node; R760xa provides 1 TB system memory and 320 GB GPU memory (80 GB × 4 GPUs) per node.

For GPU memory, the audit must identify that researcher 7 (Dr. Tanaka) requires 640 GB which exactly matches a full DGX H100 node (no overhead), and multiple researchers requiring 512 GB need at least 7 H100 GPUs (nearly a full DGX node).

For storage, the audit must note that shared storage totals 700 TB (500 TB PowerScale + 200 TB NetApp) while total storage_tb_required from computing_needs sums to 624.5 TB (89% utilization at deployment).
The audit should flag individual researchers with very high storage needs (e.g., Dr. Kowalski at 70 TB, Dr. Johansson at 50 TB) as capacity risks.

rubrics.rubric: Does the adjusted budget correctly apply the 5% procurement discount and 10% contingency to the vendor quote's upfront procurement costs without double-counting prepaid support?
criterion: The adjusted budget must take the vendor quote upfront subtotal of $2,713,000, which already includes the $185,000 prepaid three-year support contract, apply a 5% discount (reducing by $135,650 for full cluster) to get $2,577,350.
A 10% contingency must be added on the discounted amount: $2,577,350 × 1.10 = $2,835,085.
The budget must also account for sales tax and shipping appropriately.
The prepaid support contract must be counted exactly once in 3-year TCO and must not be added again as annual operating cash expense.
If recommending hybrid, specific line items should be removed with justification (e.g., reducing DGX H100 or R760xa count), with discount/contingency applied to the modified subtotal.

rubrics.rubric: Does the annual operating cost calculation correctly compute power costs using the formula: pre-PUE electrical load × PUE 1.5 × $0.09/kWh × 8,760 hours/year?
criterion: The adjusted budget must use the audit-corrected full-cluster pre-PUE electrical load of approximately 86.22 kW (68.8 kW total compute + 6.3 kW storage + 9.5 kW network + 1.62 kW UPS overhead) × PUE 1.5 = approximately 129.33 kW total facility power. The vendor's 114.2 kW figure may appear only as a clearly labeled error-sensitivity case.

Total annual energy must be approximately 129.33 kW × 8,760 hrs = 1,132,931 kWh/year, yielding approximately $101,964/year at $0.09/kWh; minor differences caused by rounding 86.22 kW to 86.2 kW are acceptable.

The operating budget must also include 2 FTE at $95K each ($190,000), licenses at $45,000, and explicitly show the three-year support contract as prepaid coverage with $0 additional cash outlay in Years 1-3.
If hybrid, the power calculation should use the reduced on-prem load plus cloud operational costs.

rubrics.rubric: Does the budget include a Summary Dashboard sheet with a break-even utilization rate calculation showing at what utilization level on-prem becomes cheaper than cloud per GPU-hour?
criterion: The Summary Dashboard sheet must compute the 3-year TCO for on-prem (capital + 3 years of operating costs) and total available GPU-hours per year using the corrected installed capacity of 64 GPUs (32 H100 + 32 A100) × 8,760 hours = 560,640 GPU-hrs/year at 100% utilization. If the vendor quote's '96 GPUs' / '7,680 GB GPU memory' aggregate is mentioned, it must be treated as a source inconsistency to be documented in the audit rather than as the budgeting baseline.
The break-even calculation must divide 3-year TCO by (3 × 560,640 × utilization rate) to get cost/GPU-hr and set this equal to the blended cloud rate to solve for utilization.

The break-even conclusion must be numerically defensible. If the corrected 64-GPU baseline implies a very high utilization threshold or no break-even below 100%, the dashboard should state that explicitly rather than forcing a 'typical' percentage.
The dashboard must also include 3-year TCO comparisons for all three strategies (on-prem, cloud-only, hybrid).

rubrics.rubric: Does the analysis correctly characterize workload-type mix and wait-time distributions from the database, highlighting severe capacity constraints for high-priority workloads?
criterion: The analysis must segment workloads from the computing_needs table by type: Model Training (18 entries, highest GPU-hours), Simulation (11 entries), Data Processing (8 entries), Inference (6 entries, low GPU-hours), and Visualization (2 entries).
The analysis must report wait time ranges: from 2 hours (Dr. Kowalczyk, Inference) to 168 hours (Dr. Kowalski, Simulation — 7 full days).
The analysis must note that many priority-5 workloads (the most critical) have extremely long wait times (72-168 hours), indicating severe capacity constraints for the most important research.

rubrics.rubric: Does the discrepancy table in the data audit include all required columns (Source_A, Source_B, Field, Value_A, Value_B, Severity, Recommended_Resolution) and correctly classify severity as Critical or Minor?
criterion: The audit must present discrepancies in a table with exactly seven columns: Source_A, Source_B, Field, Value_A, Value_B, Severity (Critical/Minor), and Recommended_Resolution.
Critical-severity items must include: the DGX H100 lead time vs. WBS scheduling conflict and power arithmetic inconsistencies affecting infrastructure planning.
Minor-severity items should include items such as UPS rounding (1.62 kW stated as 1.6 kW) and BTU/hr calculation discrepancies.
Each row must have a specific resolution recommendation, not just identification of the problem.

rubrics.rubric: Does the analysis correctly identify that the existing infrastructure (64 GPUs across 10 systems at 85-100% utilization, with two end-of-life and two degraded systems) is critically inadequate for the 75,800 GPU-hours/month demand?
criterion: The analysis must query the current_infrastructure table to establish that existing infrastructure has 64 GPUs total across 10 systems with utilization ranging from 85% to 100%, including two end-of-life systems (gpu-cluster-01, legacy-hpc-01) and two degraded systems (gpu-cluster-02, workstation-pool).

The analysis must calculate that at ~90-95% average utilization, existing systems provide roughly 64 × 730 hrs/month × 0.93 ≈ 43,500 GPU-hours/month capacity against 75,800 GPU-hours/month demand — a ~42% deficit.
The analysis must note that many existing GPUs (V100-16GB, V100-32GB, RTX-2080Ti, RTX-3090) lack the memory capacity needed for modern large-model AI workloads.
